geology_notes: Churchill Resources holds the Foxtrot past-producing antimony mine (Frost Cove / Black Raven property) in central Newfoundland, and has expanded its district land position through the March 2026 Golden Baie option (39,925 ha, TSXV-approved March 27, 2026) and a Black Raven LOI. Confirmed geological highlights from accessible disclosures: (1) FC25-27: 13.00% Sb over 0.57m at Frost Cove — validated after the May 2026 data-correction release that downgraded the broader initial assay dataset; (2) a second new polymetallic system at southern Frost Cove / Black Raven yielding 7.25% Sb over 1.98m; (3) a 20-vein Au-Ag-Mo-Pb-Zn swarm at Pomley Cove Pond with surface channel results including 17.3 g/t Au and 130 g/t Ag; (4) zinc grab samples at Black Raven reaching 5.25%, 11.03%, and 12.11% Zn with associated Au, Ag, and Pb. Nine 2026 drill holes completed circa July 13 remain without confirmed public assay release as of July 29 — sixteen days since the 'imminent' assay announcement; search results and news indices show no results headline. The August 2023 NI 43-101 technical report remains the most recent on file; its first 60 pages yielded no compliant resource estimate. All five resource/reserve fields are null per extraction. Score of 3 reflects confirmed high-grade multi-commodity mineralisation across a consolidated NL property package, constrained by absence of a compliant resource estimate and the still-pending 2026 assay results.

catalyst_notes: Macro catalyst: China's September 2024 antimony export controls restricted supply from the dominant global producer and have sustained Western-government urgency for domestic and allied critical mineral supply chains. Antimony is named in Canada's Critical Minerals Strategy and on the US Defense Production Act designated minerals list, making Foxtrot a credible candidate for NRCan/provincial grant support and strategic partnership interest. This macro tailwind remains durable as of July 29, 2026. Company-specific catalyst (adverse development confirmed): CRI shares fell approximately 20% on July 15, 2026, closing near C$0.04. The specific trigger for the decline was not independently confirmable but the timing — two days after the nine 2026 drill holes were reported as completed circa July 13 and while assay results remained pending — is notable. As of July 29 the 2026 assay batch remains without confirmed public release — sixteen days since the 'imminent' announcement; no results headline appeared in two targeted news-index searches conducted today. Score of 2: the macro tailwind remains intact but the unexplained July 15 stock decline and sixteen days of silence past an 'imminent' assay promise together erode near-term catalyst timing confidence.

The confirmed geological highlights from the 2025 campaign — 13.00% Sb over 0.57m at Frost Cove (validated May 2026), 7.25% Sb over 1.98m at a second polymetallic system, 17.3 g/t Au and 130 g/t Ag at Pomley Cove Pond veins, and up to 12.11% Zn grab samples at Black Raven — establish a credible multi-commodity exploration story across the consolidated land package. Nine 2026 drill holes completed circa July 13 remain without confirmed public assay release as of July 29 — sixteen days since the 'imminent' announcement; three targeted searches conducted today found no results headline. CRI shares fell approximately 20% on July 15, 2026, closing near C$0.04 (implied market cap roughly C$12.7M at 316.7M shares issued); the specific cause remains unconfirmed. Cap table per the April 2026 MD&A extraction: 316,681,940 shares issued and outstanding; 342,756,940 fully diluted (2,625,000 warrants + 23,450,000 options — strike prices and expiry dates unextracted). No NI 43-101 compliant resource estimate is on file; all resource/reserve fields are null. Maintain WATCH at low confidence: the critical-minerals strategic positioning with confirmed high-grade results justifies continued monitoring, but the July 15 price event and a sixteen-day assay delay past 'imminent' are near-term negative signals that prevent upgrading conviction. A results release — positive or negative — is the next binary event.
